inline.s: The ancients said, "If you would know the calamity of war in the world, you must listen to the sound of the butcher's knife at midnight." And again: "If you wish the world to be free from the calamity of war, none but living beings must cease to eat flesh." From this we know that abstaining from killing and releasing life is the fundamental way to rescue the people of the world. Therefore Great Master Zhiyi bought more than sixty places along the sea and river at Linhai, stretching for over four hundred li, to serve as ponds for releasing life. He also petitioned the court to issue a decree and erect a stele forbidding fishing and poaching; those who secretly fished were severely punished. This continued even into the Zhenguan reign of the Tang dynasty. In the second year of Qianyuan during Emperor Suzong of the Tang, an edict was issued to the whole empire, ordering every prefecture to establish ponds for releasing life. The emperor commanded Yan Zhenqing, the great calligrapher who rose to be Minister of Personnel and Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince and was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu, to compose the inscription, which was then engraved upon stone. The inscription read: "Our enlightened sovereign takes the whole world as a pond for releasing life, blessing every place. Relying upon the sustaining power of the divine mantra, he severs the stream of birth and death within the sea of afflictions. Examining the ages past, where has there ever been such a glorious deed?"

In the first year of Tianxi during Emperor Zhenzong of the Song, an edict was issued to the whole empire to establish ponds for releasing life. West Lake of Hangzhou was likewise a pond for releasing life in the Song dynasty. In the Ming, the Great Master Lianchi (Zhuhong) established ponds for releasing life at the two places Shangfang and Changshou. His treatise on abstaining from killing and releasing life circulated throughout the world. For more than three hundred years since, monks and laypeople who have admired the master's noble conduct and extended compassion to living creatures have been beyond counting.

Someone asked: The widowed, the bereaved, the orphaned, the childless, the poor and those in distress are everywhere. Why not go to their aid, and instead rush about to rescue creatures not at all related to us? Are not the urgent and the trivial set upside down here?

I replied: You do not understand the reason why the Tathagata teaches people to abstain from killing and to release life. Humans and animals, though different in form, share the same buddha-nature. They have fallen into other species because of evil karma; we have been fortunate to gain a human body because of wholesome karma. If we do not pity them but indulge ourselves in eating them, then once our blessings are spent and their retribution is exhausted, we shall have to repay it all from the beginning, and we ourselves shall be eaten by them. You should know that the great calamities of war arise entirely from the karmic effects of killing in past lives. If there were no karma of killing, even if one met with bandits, they would give rise to good thoughts and would not do him harm. How much less so with disasters such as epidemics, floods, and fires; those who abstain from killing and release life rarely encounter them. From this we know that protecting creatures is, in truth, protecting ourselves. Abstaining from killing frees one from death by heaven's hand, death at the hands of ghosts and spirits, death by robbers, and death from the mutual reprisal of enmity in the future. As for the widowed, the bereaved, the orphaned, the childless, the poor and those in distress, one should likewise aid them according to one's station and strength. Does one who abstains from killing and releases life not perform this virtue as well? Moreover, people such as the widowed, the orphaned, the poor and the distressed, though deeply to be pitied, have not yet reached the point of death. But the creatures that are destined to be eaten, if not rescued immediately, are instantly slaughtered and cooked to fill the belly.
Again he asked: The animals that are to be eaten are beyond counting. How many can you release?

I replied: You should know that the act of releasing life is in truth the supremely excellent good thought of arousing all people to protect the lives of living creatures. We hope that they will grasp the meaning of releasing life and, pitying the creatures in their hearts, be unable to bear eating them. If everyone refrains from eating them, then no one will go to catch them. Then all creatures in the air, on the land, and in the water will freely fly, walk, and swim within their own realms, so that although no one is deliberately releasing life, yet life is universally released. Is this not taking the whole world as a pond for releasing life? Even if not everyone can do this, if a single person cannot bear to eat flesh, then countless creatures of water and land are spared from slaughter, how much more when there are far more than one such person! Moreover, this cuts off, for all who now and in the future abstain from killing and release life, the evil causes of widowhood, bereavement, orphanhood, childlessness, poverty and distress, and serves as the good conditions for long life free from illness, wealth and honor, peace and happiness, the reunion of father and son, and the growing old together of husband and wife. It is also precisely to aid in advance those who would otherwise become the widowed, the orphaned, the poor and the distressed, so that in life after life they will never suffer the miseries of widowhood, orphanhood, poverty, or distress, but will long enjoy longevity, wealth, and honor. Is this not making all places blessed? How can one be indifferent to it? Consider carefully: in abstaining from killing and releasing life, is one truly rushing about for the sake of people, or for the sake of animals? And have the urgent and the trivial been turned upside down?

Outside the Jile Temple at Nanxun there had long been a pond for releasing life. Because the embankment had not been fully built, it had collapsed. Moreover, having not been dredged or deepened for many years, it was filled with silt, and good-hearted people often released life in the river. Though they meant well, the released creatures gained little benefit. Of those released in the morning, most were caught again by evening. If one is near a great river, the creatures should be released into the river; a small river is quite unsuitable for releasing life. Master Yuanlin, grieved at heart by this situation of releasing in the morning and catching at evening, planned to dredge and deepen this pond for releasing life and to build an enclosing wall around it for protection, so that people would have a place to release the creatures without their being stolen or caught, an idea most compassionate. Before the work began, Master Juesan of Putuo Mountain happened to arrive, and at a glance the two found themselves of like mind. So Master Yuanlin entrusted the affairs of the temple to him, while he himself cast aside all conditions and single-mindedly practiced the pure karma of recitation. Master Juesan, succeeding to the task of restoring the pond for releasing life, wished to complete it as quickly as possible. But because the undertaking was vast, it could not be accomplished by one person alone. Therefore he planned to raise funds from the good and faithful people of the whole town and, together with them, to complete this fine work, and so he asked me to write a preface.

I have often grieved over the cruelty of the slaughter-karma of recent times, and wished to rescue people from it but had not the strength to act. His invitation stirred my heart. I have therefore set forth in brief the true mind originally possessed alike by humans and animals, their rise and fall in accordance with karma, and the present and future retributions of killing and of protecting life. I hope that all the benefactors will together give rise to good thoughts and together contribute pure funds, so that this work may speedily be accomplished and the fish, turtles, and other released creatures may each find their proper place. The merit and benefit will be boundless and measureless. Not only will ten thousand calamities melt away like ice in this present life and a thousand auspicious omens gather like clouds; among those in ages to come who repay their debt of gratitude, who knows how many millions of millions there will be.
